pr_title: [Swap][Tests][KEP-2400] Add swap serial stress tests, improve NodeConformance tests and adapt NoSwap behavior
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature
<!--

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120798

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR does the following:
1. Havily refactors and cleans swap node-e2e tests.
2. Adapt swap NodeConformance test to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122745 which drops `UnlimitedSwap` and introduces `NoSwap` behavior.
3. Adds serial tests for swap.

To expand on (3), two serial tests are now added which validate the following scenarios:
1. `"should be able over-commit the node memory"` - a pod is deployed which stresses memory. The test expects that once the pod uses all of the node's memory some of its memory would be swapped away.
2. `"should be able to use more memory than memory limits"` - a pod with memory limits stresses memory. Eventually it goes beyond its memory limits and instead of being OOM killed some of its memory is swapped away keeping it alive.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The original version of this PR was here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120430

Due to unfortunate situations I had to be out of work for a while, therefore my PR was closed and continued here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122175

Fortunately I was able to come back to work and therefore the PR is now continued here.

issue_context.title: [KEP-2400] [Swap]: SwapConformance e2e testing
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue is a follow-up to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119430 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105025.

Currently, we have swap e2e tests. However, these tests only check that the cgroup knobs (e.g. `memory.swap.max`) had been configured properly.

This issue focuses on e2e tests that would actually get swap to kick in and would prove that over-committing the node is possible.



### Why is this needed?

KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2400-node-swap

review_comments:
Can you added documentation? Feature gate testing is one of those areas that have been misunderstood by test authors in the past.

I'll re-add LGTM and approve when done.

/lgtm cancel

Thanks @pohly!
An important comment indeed. I'm also a victim of misunderstanding how it works :)

I've added the following documentation, let me know what you think:
> // IsFeatureGateEnabled can be used during e2e tests to figure out if a certain feature gate is enabled.
> // This function is dependent on InitFeatureGates under the hood. Therefore, the test must be called with a
> // --feature-gates parameter.

/lgtm

Based on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123557#issuecomment-2120864433 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/f17c75d43d903c1e751564cfd0c739d770dbd43b..c3f16c512825c4340071efc5c90599cd6f11f77e.

/approve

For test/e2e/framework.

nevermind, that's what the variable is

```suggestion
	Swap = framework.WithNodeFeature(framework.ValidNodeFeatures.Add("SwapConformance"))
```

I think.

Not exactly.
The label you're pointing to here is for the NodeSwap feature gate. Instead I've added a `WithSwapConformance()` function to add the swap conformance label. Look at the [latest commit](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123557/commits/8a9a9617293551bddee0d4268fd7d0a71cedc1f5) for the implementation.
Thats not true. This is just the label that we use for FOCUS.

Right. That's what I meant. Let me rephrase.

We use `"NodeSwap"` at the upper `SIGDescribe`, meaning that this label appears for every swap test.
The new `"SwapConformance"` label introduced in this PR is applied only for the swap conformance tests.

This way:
- A job that focuses on NodeSwap runs all swap tests.
- A job that focuses on Serial will NOT run swap conformance.
- A job that focuses on SwapConformance will run swap conformance tests only.

Thanks for your review Sergey!

I've spent a lot of time writing these tests in a way that they will be as non-flaky and stable as possible, but at the same time will verify that every expectation from the NodeSwap feature is met. I've followed a few principles in order to achieve it:
* **The system is not configured in any special way**: The tests should work with default OS configurations to prove that NodeSwap is not dependent on any specific configuration like swappiness.
* **Tests end once the most basic functionality is verified**: For example, when ensuring that a container can exceed memory limits, the container (slowly but surely) stresses memory and once `memory.current > limits` and `memory.swap.current > 0` the test passes.

> So depending on how fast we write memory, test may start flaking.

Bear in mind that the stress is being made at a low pace to give the kernel enough time to reclaim. It is proven to be very stable until now, but we can always make it even slower if we'll see future flakiness.

I think that swappiness shouldn't matter too much here as well. Essentially it is a way to tell the kernel to prefer reclaiming file-backed memory vs anon memory, but in any case after enough stress the kernel would have to start swapping.

> The soft memory limit in cgroupv2 is something that I think may improve swap reliability.

I think you're referring to `memory.swap.high`.
